finding.title: Rename the top-level child() test helper in progress_widgets_test.dart
finding.why: A top-level function literally named `child` is called as `SingleChildScrollView(child: child(level))` (line 483) in the same file — the free function shares its name with the ubiquitous Flutter `child:` named parameter used dozens of times elsewhere in the same 583-line file, forcing a reader to disambiguate 'parameter or function?' at every occurrence.
acceptance_criteria: No top-level test helper shares a name with a common Flutter named parameter (child, key, builder, etc.)

finding.title: Complete B18 in siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart to actually exercise the unmark-after-mark ledger conflict it documents

evidence.quote:
// Then unmark the same seder — FIRST-WRITE WINS per putIfAbsent,
// so the positive mark placed first takes priority.

finding.why: B18's name and inline comments describe adding a positive seder mark then an unmark entry for the same seder, asserting the 'first (positive) mark' wins per putIfAbsent. The actual ledgerEntries list (lines 1143-1156) contains only the single positive entry -- the unmark _fakeLedgerData call described in the comment was never written -- so B18 exercises nothing beyond a trivial single-entry seder expansion already covered by B17, under a misleading name. computeLearnedLeafRefs' putIfAbsent (builder) plus getEntriesByCurriculum/getEntriesByTrack's orderBy(desc(completedAt)) (DAO) together implement a real 'most-recent-ledger-action-wins' contract with no shared documentation and no runtime assertion tying the two together; only B18b tests the mirror direction (unmark first, mark second). A regression that flips either half of that contract (e.g. a new query path that forgets the desc ordering, or a putIfAbsent that becomes an overwrite) would silently make an old bulk-mark override a later intentional unmark, and nothing in this suite would catch the positive-first/unmark-second direction.
finding.recommendation: Add the described second _fakeLedgerData(..., entryScope: 'unmark_seder') entry after the positive one in B18 and assert the leaf remains learned (mirroring B18b's assertion in the opposite order); add a doc comment on computeLearnedLeafRefs stating the newest-first ordering precondition it relies on from callers.
acceptance_criteria: B18's ledgerEntries list contains both a positive seder entry and a corresponding unmark_seder entry, and the test fails if putIfAbsent semantics regress
computeLearnedLeafRefs doc comment states its ledgerEntries-must-be-newest-first-by-completedAt precondition

finding.title: Split recent_activity_and_hierarchy_panel_l1_test.dart and siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart under the AG-3 400-line cap
finding.why: wc -l reports 1093 and 1328 lines respectively (2.7x and 3.3x the 400-line cap coding-standards.md AG-3 sets specifically because 'content past the window is invisible' to per-file agent read budgets). Both files openly bundle two unrelated lib targets (a progress screen + a cross-feature panel; a widget view + a hotspot provider file) into one file by design (own header comments), each with its own lettered coverage group -- exactly the shape AG-3 asks to be split so an agent editing one target doesn't silently miss or duplicate the sibling section's coverage.
finding.recommendation: Split along the existing A/B(/C) section boundaries into per-target files at their AG-5 mirrored paths, e.g. recent_activity_screen_l1_test.dart (progress) + hierarchy_selection_panel_test.dart (content_browsing); siyumim_timeline_view_l1_test.dart + lifetime_knowledge_providers_l1_test.dart (both progress).
acceptance_criteria: find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' no longer lists these two files
the AG-3 checker is wired into make audit per the coding-standards.md Enforce line

finding.title: Close every inMemoryDb() opened in the progress test suite via addTearDown per drift_memory.dart's documented contract
finding.rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests — no leaked/shared native resources)

evidence.quote:
/// Callers MUST `await db.close()` in `tearDown` to free the native
/// resources.

finding.why: test/helpers/drift_memory.dart states callers MUST await db.close() in tearDown; none of these three call sites do. _StubChartDataService's db (recent_activity_and_hierarchy_panel_l1_test.dart:108-112) is static/shared mutable state across every stub instance in the file and is never closed -- currently harmless only because the stub happens to override every ChartDataService method RecentActivityScreen calls today, so a future un-overridden method would silently read a DB polluted by whichever test ran first instead of failing loudly. A9's local db (line 589) is closed inline at line 653, not in addTearDown/tearDown, so any expect() failure earlier in that test (several precede it) skips the close and leaks the native handle. siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart:187 opens a brand-new native DB inside a provider-override closure invoked fresh by all 11 Part-A testWidgets, none of which close it.
finding.recommendation: Hoist each inMemoryDb() call to a local variable and register addTearDown(db.close) (or tester-level addTearDown) immediately next to it, including inside the override closure at siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart:187 and for the static stub db.
acceptance_criteria: every inMemoryDb() call site in these two files is paired with an addTearDown(...close) (or tearDown()) in the same scope
A9's db.close() executes even when an earlier expect() in the test throws

finding.title: Fix vacuous cross-feature deep-import check (Makefile check 15) and route Sacred Time's cross-feature imports through a real barrel

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

finding.why: check 15's awk does `match($0, ...)` against the WHOLE grep line (file:line:content); since the file path always starts with the importing file's own 'features/<x>/' prefix, that regex always matches the file's OWN feature name first, so a[1] (from the file path) and b[1] (also latched onto the same leading path) are always equal and the print condition never fires. I ran the exact pipeline against the current tree and confirmed 0 output despite real violations. sacred_time.dart is the feature's designated barrel but exports nothing (7 lines, no export statement) and nobody imports it; meanwhile 6 files — 1 in this batch, 5 across settings/onboarding/notifications — deep-import sacred_time internals directly (one reaches into sacred_time's data/services/ layer). coding-standards.md's current Rule 2 text also says the barrel must be named providers.dart, but no feature in the repo, including sacred_time, has ever adopted that filename — every barrel and the checker itself still use the pre-revision <feature>.dart convention, so doc and code disagree about what's even being enforced. Net effect: the one guardrail meant to bound this feature's blast radius is silently non-functional, and where it would apply is already routinely bypassed — a future sacred_time internal refactor breaks 6 unrelated files with zero warning today.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to isolate the import target (e.g. split on the quote character or operate on a field after the import keyword) before comparing feature names; then either populate sacred_time.dart's exports and migrate the 6 call sites to import through it, or accept <feature>.dart as the real convention and correct coding-standards.md's Rule 2 text to match.
acceptance_criteria: make audit check 15 flags a deliberately cross-feature-deep-import test fixture (regression-proves the awk fix)
coding-standards.md Rule 2 names the barrel filename that actually exists in the repo
sacred_time.dart either exports its public surface and is used by the 6 identified external call sites, or is removed if the feature intentionally has no barrel yet
